I took it for a proper spin, and it does what we agreed on. Signing in gets me to my own private collection, and trying to peek without being logged in just gets turned away, which is what I'd want for something private.

The things I cared about all work the way I pictured:

- Pasting a link brings back the page details for me to look over, and when a page can't be reached it still lets me save with a sensible fallback title instead of just failing.
- Trying to save something I already have stops me and points me at the one I've got — even when I typed it in a slightly different way, like different capitalization or an extra slash on the end.
- My read-later list shows only what I haven't gotten to, and checking something off clears it out.
- Setting things aside with archive takes them out of my normal view but keeps them safe, and I can pull them back.
- Marking favorites, filtering down by a couple of tags at once, searching an exact phrase in quotes, and sorting by name or date each way all behave.
- I can pull my whole collection out as both a browser-friendly file and a full backup, and the import is there for bringing things in.
- And the tag suggestions I asked about are there.

Saved copies of pages we already agreed to hold for a later round, so I'm not counting that against this. I'm happy with what you've delivered — this is the bookmark manager I asked for. Consider it accepted.
